label: Anne Shirley
value: Mrs. Allan serves as a trusted friend to Anne Shirley.
unit: Mrs. Allan serves as a trusted friend, minister's wife, and Sunday school teacher to Anne Shirley. Their relationship began on a warm note despite an early mishap where Anne accidentally flavored a layer cake with liniment, a blunder Mrs. Allan handled with gracious kindness by comforting the embarrassed girl. Over time, Anne continues to adore Mrs. Allan, enjoying hosted visits to the manse and seeking her companionship as she matures through her school years.

label: Appearance
value: Anne is tall.
unit: Anne is a tall, slender girl who possesses a pointed face, delicate features, and a slim, milk-white throat. Her facial features include luminous, starry gray eyes alongside a nose with seven distinct freckles, which are fewer than she previously had, and cheeks that display pale, everchanging roses. She has a ruddy, red hair color that has been described as auburn or splendid Titian, styled at times in long braids, smooth ripples, unbraided streaming strands, or shingled closely as short green hair. Over time, her thin figure and ungracefully long legs have grown tall enough to surpass Aunt Josephine in height.

label: History
value: Anne Shirley was born an orphan in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia.
unit: Anne Shirley was born an orphan in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia, and spent a lonely childhood being shifted between overworked families to care for children before living in an asylum for four months. She was eventually adopted out of the asylum by Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert of Green Gables, though Marilla was initially shocked because they had requested a boy. Despite early missteps, including a passionate outburst at neighbor Rachel Lynde and an accidental intoxication of her new friend Diana Barry, Anne quickly won over the Cuthberts and was permitted to stay. In school, after a classmate named Gilbert Blythe teased her red hair by calling her 'Carrots,' Anne smashed a slate over his head, sparking a fierce academic rivalry and personal feud that lasted for years. Her childhood was marked by intense imaginations and dramatic misadventures, such as accidentally dying her hair green, getting trapped on a leaking boat while re-enacting a poem, and accidentally serving anodyne liniment cake to the minister's wife. Over time, her devotion to her studies under her teacher Miss Stacy paid off when she tied with Gilbert for first place on the island's entrance exams to Queen's Academy. After graduating from Queen's with the prestigious Avery scholarship, tragedy struck when Matthew died of sudden heart failure following a bank collapse. To keep Marilla from losing her home and failing eyesight, Anne selflessly gave up her college scholarship to remain at Green Gables as the Avonlea schoolteacher, prompting Gilbert to give up his teaching post in town so she could take it; this act of kindness finally broke their feud and formed a deep friendship between them. Over her two years of teaching in Avonlea, Anne co-founded the Village Improvement Society, helped Marilla raise the orphaned Keith twins, Davy and Dora, and inadvertently sold her neighbor Mr. Harrison's cow by mistake. She also formed a cherished friendship with Miss Lavendar Lewis, ultimately helping reunite Miss Lavendar with her long-lost love, Stephen Irving. When Rachel Lynde moved into Green Gables following her husband's death, Marilla's home and sight were secured, allowing Anne to resign her teaching post to attend Redmond College alongside her childhood friends.

unit: Anne Shirley was born an orphan in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia, and spent a lonely childhood being shifted between overworked families to care for children before living in an asylum for four months. She was eventually adopted out of the asylum by Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert of Green Gables, though Marilla was initially shocked because they had requested a boy. Despite early missteps, including a passionate outburst at neighbor Rachel Lynde and an accidental intoxication of her new friend Diana Barry, Anne quickly won over the Cuthberts and was permitted to stay. In school, after a classmate named Gilbert Blythe teased her red hair by calling her 'Carrots,' Anne smashed a slate over his head, sparking a fierce academic rivalry and personal feud that lasted for years. Her childhood was marked by intense imaginations and dramatic misadventures, such as accidentally dying her hair green, getting trapped on a leaking boat while re-enacting a poem, and accidentally serving anodyne liniment cake to the minister's wife. Over time, her devotion to her studies under her teacher Miss Stacy paid off when she tied with Gilbert for first place on the island's entrance exams to Queen's Academy. After graduating from Queen's with the prestigious Avery scholarship, tragedy struck when Matthew died of sudden heart failure following a bank collapse. To keep Marilla from losing her home and failing eyesight, Anne selflessly gave up her college scholarship to remain at Green Gables as the Avonlea schoolteacher, prompting Gilbert to give up his teaching post in town so she could take it; this act of kindness finally broke their feud and formed a deep friendship between them. Over her two years of teaching in Avonlea, Anne co-founded the Village Improvement Society, helped Marilla raise the orphaned Keith twins, Davy and Dora, and inadvertently sold her neighbor Mr. Harrison's cow by mistake. She also formed a cherished friendship with Miss Lavendar Lewis, ultimately helping reunite Miss Lavendar with her long-lost love, Stephen Irving. When Rachel Lynde moved into Green Gables following her husband's death, Marilla's home and sight were secured, allowing Anne to resign her teaching post to attend Redmond College alongside her childhood friends.

unit: Anne Shirley was born an orphan in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia, and spent a lonely childhood being shifted between overworked families to care for children before living in an asylum for four months. She was eventually adopted out of the asylum by Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert of Green Gables, though Marilla was initially shocked because they had requested a boy. Despite early missteps, including a passionate outburst at neighbor Rachel Lynde and an accidental intoxication of her new friend Diana Barry, Anne quickly won over the Cuthberts and was permitted to stay. In school, after a classmate named Gilbert Blythe teased her red hair by calling her 'Carrots,' Anne smashed a slate over his head, sparking a fierce academic rivalry and personal feud that lasted for years. Her childhood was marked by intense imaginations and dramatic misadventures, such as accidentally dying her hair green, getting trapped on a leaking boat while re-enacting a poem, and accidentally serving anodyne liniment cake to the minister's wife. Over time, her devotion to her studies under her teacher Miss Stacy paid off when she tied with Gilbert for first place on the island's entrance exams to Queen's Academy. After graduating from Queen's with the prestigious Avery scholarship, tragedy struck when Matthew died of sudden heart failure following a bank collapse. To keep Marilla from losing her home and failing eyesight, Anne selflessly gave up her college scholarship to remain at Green Gables as the Avonlea schoolteacher, prompting Gilbert to give up his teaching post in town so she could take it; this act of kindness finally broke their feud and formed a deep friendship between them. Over her two years of teaching in Avonlea, Anne co-founded the Village Improvement Society, helped Marilla raise the orphaned Keith twins, Davy and Dora, and inadvertently sold her neighbor Mr. Harrison's cow by mistake. She also formed a cherished friendship with Miss Lavendar Lewis, ultimately helping reunite Miss Lavendar with her long-lost love, Stephen Irving. When Rachel Lynde moved into Green Gables following her husband's death, Marilla's home and sight were secured, allowing Anne to resign her teaching post to attend Redmond College alongside her childhood friends.

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "You would cry, too, if you were an orphan and had come to a place you thought was going to be home and found that they didn’t want you because you weren’t a boy. Oh, this is the most tragical thing that ever happened to me!"

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "but, oh, please do call me Cordelia. It can’t matter much to you what you call me if I’m only going to be here a little while, can it? And Anne is such an unromantic name."

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "why didn’t you tell me at the station that you didn’t want me and leave me there? If I hadn’t seen the White Way of Delight and the Lake of Shining Waters it wouldn’t be so hard."

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "She brought Lily Jones for herself. Lily is only five years old and she is very beautiful and had nut-brown hair. If I was very beautiful and had nut-brown hair would you keep me?"

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "Pretty well. I’m better at looking after children, though. I’ve had so much experience at that. It’s such a pity you haven’t any here for me to look after."

value: Charlotta the Fourth served as a helper to Miss Lavendar Lewis.
unit: Charlotta the Fourth served as a helper to Miss Lavendar Lewis at her secluded home, Echo Lodge. While picking wild strawberries with Anne Shirley, Charlotta confided her concerns about Miss Lavendar's listlessness and recent change in behavior. Later, Charlotta helped Anne prepare a nervous Miss Lavendar for the arrival of her long-lost love, Stephen Irving, and witnessed their happy reunion from the kitchen. In the following weeks, Charlotta assisted Anne and Diana with the preparations leading up to Miss Lavendar and Stephen's garden wedding.

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: "it’s plain to be seen you and Miss Lavendar have got a secret and I think, begging your pardon if I’m too forward, Miss Shirley, ma’am, that it’s real mean not to tell me when we’ve all been such chums."

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: "But I’m sure I shan’t sleep a blessed wink, Miss Shirley, ma’am, for fear that something’ll go wrong at the last minute . . . the cream won’t whip . . . or Mr. Irving’ll have a stroke and not be able to come."

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: "but there’s so much to do yet . . . and oh, Miss Shirley, ma’am, I’m skeered it’s going to rain and I wish you’d get up and tell me you think it ain’t."

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: "I peeked from the kitchen window . . . and he’s awful handsome . . . and just the right age for Miss Lavendar. And oh, Miss Shirley, ma’am, do you think it would be much harm to listen at the door?"

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: "Yes, ma’am. Come in, ma’am. I’ll tell Miss Lavendar you’re here, ma’am. She’s upstairs, ma’am."

His early antics included tricking Dora into a pigpen, placing a toad in Marilla's bed, and locking Dora inside a toolhouse, though he eventually broke down in remorse when confronted by Anne Shirley. Davy formed a close bond with Anne, who regularly corrected his funny theological misunderstandings, comforted his occasional jealousy, and guided him through bedtime prayers. When the twins' uncle passed away, he left behind a trust fund that officially secured Davy's permanent home at Green Gables.

Davy formed a close bond with Anne, who regularly corrected his funny theological misunderstandings, comforted his occasional jealousy, and guided him through bedtime prayers. Despite continuing to cause minor mishaps, such as accidentally ruining lemon pies prepared for a guest and misbehaving at table and in school, he was openly preferred by Marilla and Anne over his sister due to his lively nature. When the twins' uncle passed away, he left behind a trust fund that officially secured Davy's permanent home at Green Gables.

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: "You don’t look like a lady who’d whip a little boy just ’cause he couldn’t keep still. Didn’t you find it awful hard to keep still when you was only ‘s old as me?"

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: "You was a girl once, I s’pose, though it’s awful funny to think of it. Dora can sit still . . . but there ain’t much fun in it I don’t think. Seems to me it must be slow to be a girl. Here, Dora, let me liven you up a bit."

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: "Marilla washed it yesterday . . . and Mrs. Wiggins scoured me with hard soap the day of the funeral. That’s enough for one week. I don’t see the good of being so awful clean. It’s lots more comfable being dirty."

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: "But it was such a jolly big caterpillar . . . I picked him up on the church steps just as we went in. It seemed a pity to waste him. And say, wasn’t it fun to hear that girl yell?"

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: “I . . . did something else today,” went on Davy in a muffled voice. “I’m sorry now but I’m awful scared to tell you. You won’t be very cross, will you? And you won’t tell Marilla, will you?”

label: History
value: Diana Barry formed an immediate, fast friendship with Anne Shirley.
unit: Diana Barry formed an immediate, fast friendship with Anne Shirley upon meeting her at Orchard Slope, solemnizing their bond with a garden oath. Their play was temporarily disrupted when Mrs. Barry forbade Diana from seeing Anne after an incident involving Anne's imaginative antics, leaving the girls to share a dramatic goodbye and secret notes until Anne nursed Diana's younger sister, Minnie May, through a severe case of croup. Restored to her friend's side, Diana hosted a party where Anne broke her ankle, and she later brought Anne the news that Anne had tied for first place on the island in the Queen's Entrance exams. Together, Diana and Anne helped establish the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, actively canvassing their neighbors for funds, attempting to prevent offensive fence advertisements, and enduring community mishaps such as a local hall being accidentally painted bright blue. During their strolls, Diana shared local lore, such as the poignant story behind Hester Gray's hidden garden, and helped host visiting guests like Mrs. Charlotte E. Morgan. On a walk to West Grafton, the two girls lost their way and discovered Echo Lodge, befriending its secluded resident, Miss Lavendar Lewis. When Anne later prepared to leave Avonlea for Redmond College, Diana expressed her deep anxiety about their upcoming separation and sought reassurance about Anne's feelings for Gilbert Blythe. Shortly before Miss Lavendar's wedding, Anne discovered Diana's secret romance with Fred Wright, after which Diana visited Green Gables to confide her engagement to her best friend.

label: History
value: Dora is an orphan.
unit: Dora was an orphaned twin who was brought to Green Gables by Marilla alongside her brother Davy, whose wild behavior contrasted with her own perfect conduct. Early on, Davy subjected her to various tricks, including pushing her into a pigpen and later locking her inside Mr. Harrison's toolhouse, where Anne eventually rescued her after a frantic search. Despite her quiet and well-behaved demeanor, both Anne and Marilla privately admitted to preferring her mischievous brother over her. Following the death of their uncle Richard Keith, a trust fund was established for Dora and Davy, guaranteeing that they could remain permanently at Green Gables.

label: History
value: Harrison moved to Avonlea.
unit: After moving to Avonlea, Harrison first met Anne Shirley when he furiously confronted her over her cow breaking into his oats. Their rocky start was soon resolved when Anne accidentally sold his Jersey cow and came to apologize, after which Harrison accepted her cake and invited her to tea. Although he developed a warm friendship with Anne, he remained skeptical of her gentle teaching methods and flatly refused to contribute to her Village Improvement Society. Later, a devastating hail storm struck the village, leaving Harrison grieving the loss of his beloved parrot, Ginger. His life was upended again when his estranged wife, Emily, unexpectedly arrived in Avonlea; Harrison confessed to Anne that they had previously separated over household arguments and Ginger, but he admitted he was glad to reconcile with her. Following their reunion, Harrison remained a regular part of Anne's life, hosting her for visits prior to local events like Miss Lavendar's wedding.

Their rocky start was soon resolved when Anne accidentally sold his Jersey cow and came to apologize, after which Harrison accepted her cake and invited her to tea. Although he developed a warm friendship with Anne, he remained skeptical of her gentle teaching methods and flatly refused to contribute to her Village Improvement Society. Later, a devastating hail storm struck the village, leaving Harrison grieving the loss of his beloved parrot, Ginger. His life was upended again when his estranged wife, Emily, unexpectedly arrived in Avonlea; Harrison confessed to Anne that they had previously separated over household arguments and Ginger, but he admitted he was glad to reconcile with her. Following their reunion, Harrison remained a regular part of Anne's life, hosting her for visits prior to local events like Miss Lavendar's wedding.

label: Quote
value: Harrison said: "Sorry, miss! Sorry isn’t going to help matters any. You’d better go and look at the havoc that animal has made in my oats . . . trampled them from center to circumference, miss."

label: Quote
value: Harrison said: “Who? Mrs. Lynde? Don’t you tell me I’m like that old gossip,” said Mr. Harrison irritably. “I’m not . . . not a bit. What have you got in that box?”

label: Quote
value: Harrison said: "I don’t, that’s a fact, and I’m mighty fond of it, too. I’m much obliged to you. It looks good on top. I hope it’s good all the way through."

label: Quote
value: Harrison said: "Well, I’ll tell you what, miss, you must help me eat it. I’ll put the kettle on and we’ll have a cup of tea. How will that do?"

label: Quote
value: Harrison said: "I see you haven’t much confidence in my ability to make tea. You’re wrong . . . I can brew up as good a jorum of tea as you ever drank. But go ahead yourself. Fortunately it rained last Sunday, so there’s plenty of clean dishes."

label: History
value: Jane Andrews spent her youth in Avonlea.
unit: Jane Andrews spent her youth in Avonlea, where she attended school alongside Anne Shirley and engaged in social outings, including riding home with Anne and Diana after a charity concert at the White Sands Hotel. As she grew older, Jane pursued higher education at Queen's Academy in the same class as her peers. After completing her studies, she joined her fellow young teachers, such as Anne and Gilbert Blythe, in debating pedagogical approaches on the eve of their first teaching positions. As an active community member, Jane joined the Avonlea Village Improvement Society and assisted Anne and Diana in canvassing neighbors to support local causes. She also helped protect the town's scenery when she accompanied Anne and Diana to confront Judson Parker about renting his fences for advertisements.

label: History
value: Jane Andrews joined a story club.
unit: Jane Andrews joined a story club alongside her friends and excelled in her education, passing the Entrance examinations and eventually taking home economics honors at Queen's Academy before teaching school at Newbridge. During her time in school, she visited Anne at her boarding house and shared the news about the Avery scholarship. She later joined Anne, Diana, and Priscilla on a memorable spring walk through the woods to discover Hester Gray's old garden. As an active member of the local Improvement Society, Jane also joined Anne and Diana in an unsuccessful attempt to persuade Judson Parker not to rent his fence to a patent medicine company for advertising.

label: History
value: Josephine Barry is an elderly resident of Charlottetown.
unit: Josephine Barry, an elderly resident of Charlottetown, first encountered Anne Shirley at Orchard Slope after Anne and Diana accidentally jumped on her in a spare-room bed. Though initially enraged to the point of planning an early departure and canceling Diana's music lessons, Miss Barry was thoroughly charmed by Anne's sincere apology and imaginative nature, choosing to stay in Avonlea and become her lifelong friend. She later hosted Anne and Diana at her town home, Beechwood, during the local Exhibition, and continued to offer hospitality and support to Anne during her time studying at Queen's Academy. Proud of Anne's achievements, Miss Barry attended her commencement ceremony to celebrate her winning the Avery scholarship. Later, when Anne needed a specific item, Miss Barry sent out a willowware platter from her collection, having paid twenty dollars for it and warning Anne to care for it properly.

label: History
value: Josie Pye attended the Avonlea school
unit: Josie Pye attended the Avonlea school as the last member of her family to go there. Possessing a natural gift for walking board fences, she used her skill to challenge Anne Shirley during a game of dares at Diana's party, daring Anne to walk the ridgepole of the kitchen roof. Josie was also known for her needlework talents, having won first prize for knitted lace at an exhibition. Later in her schooling, she traveled to town alongside her Avonlea classmates to take the Entrance examinations for Queen's Academy. After passing, she attended Queen's Academy in town along with her peers. During her time there, Josie visited Anne Shirley alongside Jane and Ruby to share news of the Avery scholarship.

Josie was also known for her needlework talents, having won first prize for knitted lace at an exhibition. Later in her schooling, she traveled to town alongside her Avonlea classmates to take the Entrance examinations for Queen's Academy. After passing, she attended Queen's Academy in town along with her peers. During her time there, Josie visited Anne Shirley alongside Jane and Ruby to share news of the Avery scholarship.

value: Judson Parker was an Avonlea resident.
unit: Judson Parker was an Avonlea resident who consistently voted for Grant in elections. When he planned to rent his barn fence to a patent medicine company for advertising, members of the Village Improvement Society were appalled and attempted to persuade him to reconsider. Though he initially refused their requests, Judson agreed to cancel the advertising contract after Anne Shirley accidentally overheard him accepting a political bribe from Jerry Corcoran and leveraged her silence to protect his reputation.

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "But oh, won’t you stay and have tea with me? Please, do. Mr. Kimball’s will have tea over before you get there. And Charlotta the Fourth and I will be so glad to have you."

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "I love them myself. They are very good company . . . with a little pretending. On calm evenings Charlotta the Fourth and I often sit out here and amuse ourselves with them. Charlotta, take back the horn and hang it carefully in its place."

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "It gave me a shock to hear about Stephen’s son that first day you were here, Anne. I’ve never been able to mention him to you since, but I’ve wanted to know all about him. What sort of a boy is he?"

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "About your age I think. He ought to be older because I dreamed him long before you were born. But I’ll never let him get any older than eleven or twelve; because if I did some day he might grow up altogether and then I’d lose him."

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "I’m wholesomely ashamed to think that a new dress . . . even it is a forget-me-not organdy . . . should exhilarate me so, when a good conscience and an extra contribution to Foreign Missions couldn’t do it."

label: Personality
value: Marilla Cuthbert is a self-contained woman.
unit: A self-contained and determined woman, Marilla Cuthbert possesses a sensible, pragmatic outlook and views the world purely through prose. She is characterized by a narrow experience and a rigid conscience, detesting stinginess in children while scorning poetic weakness. Although she maintains a neat, order-loving household, her uncomfortable ignorance can occasionally make her crisp, curt, and somewhat sarcastic, particularly when suffering from headaches. By nature and habit, she remains stoic and reserved in expressing her affection, finding it difficult to put her deep feelings into words. Additionally, she is celebrated locally for her skill in making three-year-old homemade currant wine, and she motivated herself to keep a pair of twins despite concerns over whether she could afford to do so.

Although she maintains a neat, order-loving household, her uncomfortable ignorance can occasionally make her crisp, curt, and somewhat sarcastic, particularly when suffering from headaches. By nature and habit, she remains stoic and reserved in expressing her affection, finding it difficult to put her deep feelings into words. Additionally, she is celebrated locally for her skill in making three-year-old homemade currant wine, and she motivated herself to keep a pair of twins despite concerns over whether she could afford to do so.

label: History
value: Matthew returned from the train station with a young girl named Anne.
unit: When Marilla Cuthbert sent Matthew to the train station to fetch an orphan boy from Nova Scotia, he returned instead with a young girl named Anne, shocking Marilla. Though initially determined to return the child, Marilla felt deep pity upon hearing Anne's difficult past, refused to pass her to a harsh neighbor, and agreed to adopt her, resolving to educate her properly. She raised Anne with a mixture of stern discipline and affection, managing her outbursts, eccentric prayers, and various mishaps, such as when Anne dyed her hair green or accidentally served currant wine to her friend Diana. Though often exasperated by Anne's antics, Marilla grew deeply fond of her and felt profound pride in the girl's achievements as she excelled in school. When Matthew tragically died of heart failure and an oculist warned Marilla that her failing eyesight meant giving up reading and sewing, she considered selling Green Gables. However, Anne gave up her college scholarship to stay home, care for Marilla, and teach locally. Marilla later agreed to temporarily foster two orphaned twins, Davy and Dora, whose uncle subsequently passed away and left a trust fund that allowed them to stay permanently at Green Gables. Despite the chaotic challenges of raising the mischievous Davy alongside Dora, Marilla found herself growing attached to the boy. When her long-time neighbor Rachel Lynde lost her husband, Marilla invited Mrs. Lynde to move into Green Gables, a living arrangement that freed Anne to leave and pursue her dream of attending Redmond College.

label: Quote
value: Marilla Cuthbert said: "I’d never dream of taking a girl to bring up. I wonder at Mrs. Alexander Spencer for doing it. But there, she wouldn’t shrink from adopting a whole orphan asylum if she took it into her head."

label: Quote
value: Marilla Cuthbert said: "No. We want a boy to help Matthew on the farm. A girl would be of no use to us. Take off your hat. I’ll lay it and your bag on the hall table."

label: Quote
value: Marilla Cuthbert said: "Well, undress as quick as you can and go to bed. I’ll come back in a few minutes for the candle. I daren’t trust you to put it out yourself. You’d likely set the place on fire."

label: Quote
value: Marilla Cuthbert said: "I don’t feel as if I wanted any more children to look after than I’ve got at present. You’re problem enough in all conscience. What’s to be done with you I don’t know. Matthew is a most ridiculous man."

label: Quote
value: Marilla Cuthbert said: "We’re not talking about poetry, Anne—we are talking about saying your prayers. Don’t you know it’s a terrible wicked thing not to say your prayers every night? I’m afraid you are a very bad little girl."

Following his father's sudden arrival in town and subsequent reconciliation with Miss Lavendar, Paul shared in the excitement leading up to their wedding. He ultimately attended the outdoor ceremony in the garden to celebrate his father and Miss Lavendar's marriage before they departed.

Following his father's sudden arrival in town and subsequent reconciliation with Miss Lavendar, Paul shared in the excitement leading up to their wedding. He ultimately attended the outdoor ceremony in the garden to celebrate his father and Miss Lavendar's marriage before they departed.

value: Paul Irving said: "you can’t think what has happened! Something so splendid. Father is here . . . just think of that! Father is here! Come right in. Father, this is my beautiful teacher. You know, father."

value: Paul Irving said: “Yes; but if dryads are foolish they must take the consequences, just as if they were real people,” said Paul gravely. “Do you know what I think about the new moon, teacher? I think it is a little golden boat full of dreams.”

label: Personality
value: Rachel Lynde is a kind woman.
unit: Rachel Lynde is a kind, hardworking, and capable woman who is known for her observant nature and deep involvement as an active worker in her church. Exceptionally managing, she handles her own affairs alongside those of others, though her penchant for curiosity means few occurrences in Avonlea escape her notice. She prides herself on speaking her mind without fear or favor, offering advice that can be aggressive or scorching despite her good heart and willingness to admit her own mistakes. A skilled sewer and dedicated, tender nurse, she holds a pessimistic outlook on life's disappointments yet remains firmly devoted to her home, preferring to live anywhere in Avonlea over leaving it.

label: History
value: Mrs. Rachel Lynde was a long-time resident of Avonlea.
unit: Mrs. Rachel Lynde was a long-time resident of Avonlea who had lived as Marilla Cuthbert's neighbor for forty-five years without a quarrel. Intrigued when Matthew Cuthbert dressed up and drove away, she visited Green Gables and was thoroughly shocked to learn the Cuthberts were adopting an orphan boy. When Anne Shirley arrived instead, Mrs. Rachel visited and bluntly criticized her appearance, prompting Anne to explode at her; however, after Anne delivered a dramatic apology at her home, Mrs. Rachel readily forgiven her. Over time, she assisted the Green Gables household, such as when Matthew enlisted her help to select and sew a modern dress with puffed sleeves for Anne. She monitored local affairs closely, cautioning Anne against starting a Village Improvement Society and later discovering that the local hall had been painted bright blue due to a paint mix-up. After her husband Thomas passed away, Mrs. Rachel accepted Marilla's invitation to move into Green Gables, an arrangement that freed Anne to leave teaching and attend Redmond College.

Intrigued when Matthew Cuthbert dressed up and drove away, she visited Green Gables and was thoroughly shocked to learn the Cuthberts were adopting an orphan boy. When Anne Shirley arrived instead, Mrs. Rachel visited and bluntly criticized her appearance, prompting Anne to explode at her; however, after Anne delivered a dramatic apology at her home, Mrs. Rachel readily forgiven her. Over time, she assisted the Green Gables household, such as when Matthew enlisted her help to select and sew a modern dress with puffed sleeves for Anne. She monitored local affairs closely, cautioning Anne against starting a Village Improvement Society and later discovering that the local hall had been painted bright blue due to a paint mix-up. After her husband Thomas passed away, Mrs. Rachel accepted Marilla's invitation to move into Green Gables, an arrangement that freed Anne to leave teaching and attend Redmond College.

label: Quote
value: Rachel Lynde said: "She’s terrible skinny and homely, Marilla. Come here, child, and let me have a look at you. Lawful heart, did any one ever see such freckles? And hair as red as carrots! Come here, child, I say."

label: Quote
value: Rachel Lynde said: "I just guess she has done well, and far be it from me to be backward in saying it. You’re a credit to your friends, Anne, that’s what, and we’re all proud of you."

label: Quote
value: Rachel Lynde said: "Child, yes, I’m afraid of it. Look at his face. When you’ve seen that look as often as I have you’ll know what it means."

label: Quote
value: Rachel Lynde said: "I saw Mr. Harrison chasing your Jersey out of his oats today when I was coming home from Carmody. I thought he looked pretty mad. Did he make much of a rumpus?"

label: Quote
value: Rachel Lynde said: "And every one of them said they liked you splendid, Anne, except Anthony Pye. I must admit he didn’t. He said you ‘weren’t any good, just like all girl teachers.’ There’s the Pye leaven for you. But never mind."

value: Ruby Gillis is cheerful.

She is heavily focused on young men and romantic attention, frequently speaking about boys and the compliments she receives. Her main ambitions involve having numerous suitors captivated by her, securing a romantic partner by age fifteen, and teaching for only two years before getting married.

label: History
value: Ruby Gillis attended school with Anne Shirley.
unit: Growing up alongside Anne Shirley, Ruby Gillis attended school and Queen's Academy with her. As a young girl, she declared her intention to have dozens of beaus when she grew up, a pursuit that later yielded numerous suitors and fueled local gossip. Among her admirers, Nelson Atkins proposed to her, though he did so using a line copied from an etiquette book; upon discovering this, Ruby went home and wrote him a scathing refusal.

label: History
value: Sarah was forbidden by her father from marrying Luther Wallace twenty years ago
unit: Sarah was forbidden by her father from marrying Luther Wallace twenty years ago because Luther was poor, leaving her to whitewash an old duckhouse every spring in case it ever proved useful. Years later, she rescued Anne Shirley after the girl became stuck on her duckhouse roof while trying to peek into her pantry window. After accepting Anne's apology, Sarah negotiated the sale of her old willow-ware platter for twenty-five dollars and revealed that she was planning to get married.

Maintaining perfect order without ever whipping her students, she confirmed she would return for a second year of teaching. Throughout the following school year, Miss Stacy provided careful guidance to prepare Anne and her classmates for the Queen's Entrance examination, even accompanying them to town to sit for the test.

label: History
value: Twenty-five years prior, Stephen Irving became engaged to Lavendar Lewis.
unit: Twenty-five years prior, Stephen Irving became engaged to Lavendar Lewis, but their romance ended in a falling-out, leading Stephen to go away to the States and never return home. Decades later, his son Paul met Miss Lavendar and bonded with her, setting the stage for Stephen's eventual sudden arrival back in town. Upon his return, Stephen visited Anne Shirley and asked her to relay a message to Miss Lavendar before going to Echo Lodge himself. He happily reunited with Miss Lavendar in her garden, and the two were subsequently married there in the presence of family and friends before departing at the station.

value: Stephen Irving said: "In Paul’s last letter he spoke of going with you to visit an old . . . friend of mine . . . Miss Lewis at the stone house in Grafton. Do you know her well?"

label: v2 · VIII Marilla Adopts Twins
value: Marilla arrives home.
chapter: v2 · VIII Marilla Adopts Twins
unit: Marilla arrives home with the orphaned Keith twins, Davy and Dora, whose contrasting behaviors quickly manifest during dinner and bedtime. Davy creates chaos throughout his first week, first by dropping a caterpillar down a girl's neck at church and later by tricking Dora into falling into a pigpen before attempting to pump water on her. After being sent to bed, Davy confesses to Anne that he also placed a toad in Marilla's bed, which Anne frantically removes.

label: v1 · CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
value: Anne returns from her last day of school
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
unit: Anne returns from her last day of school crying over Mr. Phillips's departure, despite her mixed feelings about him, and reports meeting Avonlea's new minister, Mr. Allan, and his wife. She later discusses the new minister with Matthew and Marilla, falls in love with Mrs. Allan as her new Sunday school teacher, and eagerly prepares to host the couple for tea at Green Gables. After preparing a layer cake and decorating the table, Anne watches in anticipation as Mrs. Allan and Marilla take their first bite of the cake, only for Marilla to react in shock.

unit: Anne decorates the tea table beautifully for the minister and his wife, and even manages to get Matthew to sit with them and talk. However, disaster strikes when Mrs. Allan eats the layer cake Anne made and realizes it has been flavored with anodyne liniment instead of vanilla. Mortified, Anne retreats to her room in tears, but Mrs. Allan kindly comforts her and turns the mistake into a lighthearted moment.

Afterwards, Marilla and Matthew discuss Anne's growth and secretly express their deep pride in her performance and future potential.

Over the course of the school year, she prepares for the Queen's Entrance examination under Miss Stacy's guidance and notices her own personal growth. Marilla and Matthew reflect on how tall and mature Anne has grown, while Anne struggles with her anxieties about passing the upcoming exams.

value: Anne is in an irritable mood caused by a toothache.
chapter: v2 · XII A Jonah Day
unit: In an irritable mood caused by a toothache, Anne has a terrible day at school, accidentally causing fireworks to explode in the classroom and later whipping Anthony Pye for putting a mouse in her desk. Returning home in despair, she confesses to Marilla, who comforts her and reassures her that everyone makes mistakes. The next day, Anne is amazed to find that whipping Anthony actually won his respect, a fact later confirmed by Mrs. Lynde.

chapter: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
unit: After a newspaper item pokes fun at Uncle Abe's weather predictions, a sudden and devastating severe hail storm hits Avonlea on the exact day predicted. Anne and Marilla weather the storm at Green Gables with the twins, only to find extensive damage to crops, trees, and windows across the village. Mr. Harrison grieves the loss of his parrot Ginger, and Gilbert later visits Green Gables as the community takes stock of the destruction.

value: Anne has an irritable mood caused by a toothache.
chapter: v2 · XII A Jonah Day
unit: In an irritable mood caused by a toothache, Anne has a terrible day at school, accidentally causing fireworks to explode in the classroom and later whipping Anthony Pye for putting a mouse in her desk. Returning home in despair, she confesses to Marilla, who comforts her and reassures her that everyone makes mistakes. The next day, Anne is amazed to find that whipping Anthony actually won his respect, a fact later confirmed by Mrs. Lynde.

chapter: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
unit: After a newspaper item pokes fun at Uncle Abe's weather predictions, a sudden and devastating severe hail storm hits Avonlea on the exact day predicted. Anne and Marilla weather the storm at Green Gables with the twins, only to find extensive damage to crops, trees, and windows across the village. Mr. Harrison grieves the loss of his parrot Ginger, and Gilbert later visits Green Gables as the community takes stock of the destruction.

value: Anne and Diana discuss their plans
chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: Anne and Diana discuss their plans for the Improvement Society while driving home from Carmody. Spotting a cow in Mr. Harrison's grain field, Anne hastily sells it to Mr. Shearer thinking it is her own cow, Dolly. Upon returning to Green Gables, Anne discovers Dolly is still in the pen and realizes she sold Mr. Harrison's cow by mistake, leading her to set off to apologize with a peace-offering cake.

label: v2 · IX A Question of Color
value: Anne discusses with Mr. Harrison
chapter: v2 · IX A Question of Color
unit: Anne discusses Mrs. Lynde, truthfulness, and the Village Improvement Society's hall project with Mr. Harrison. Shortly after Joshua Pye finishes painting the hall, Mrs. Lynde discovers it was accidentally painted bright blue instead of green due to a mix-up with the paint numbers. Although the society members are devastated, the incident earns them widespread sympathy from the Avonlea community.

unit: Marilla learns from an oculist that she must give up reading and sewing to save her failing eyesight, leading her to consider selling Green Gables. Anne decides to give up her college scholarship to stay home, care for Marilla, and teach at the local school. After learning that Gilbert Blythe gave up the Avonlea school position for her benefit, Anne reconciles with him, and they agree to become close friends.

value: Anne, Jane, and Gilbert debate teaching methods.
chapter: v2 · IV Different Opinions
unit: On the eve of the school year, Anne, Jane, and Gilbert debate teaching methods, particularly whether corporal punishment is ever justified. Anne walks home, stops to visit Mr. Harrison—who also doubts her gentle discipline approach—and goes to bed feeling anxious about her first day as a teacher. The next morning, Marilla comforts Anne and gives her advice before she sets off.

label: v2 · IX A Question of Color
value: Anne discusses with Mrs. Lynde
chapter: v2 · IX A Question of Color
unit: Anne discusses Mrs. Lynde, truthfulness, and the Village Improvement Society's hall project with Mr. Harrison. Shortly after Joshua Pye finishes painting the hall, Mrs. Lynde discovers it was accidentally painted bright blue instead of green due to a mix-up with the paint numbers. Although the society members are devastated, the incident earns them widespread sympathy from the Avonlea community.

label: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
value: A newspaper item pokes fun at Uncle Abe's weather predictions.
chapter: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
unit: After a newspaper item pokes fun at Uncle Abe's weather predictions, a sudden and devastating severe hail storm hits Avonlea on the exact day predicted. Anne and Marilla weather the storm at Green Gables with the twins, only to find extensive damage to crops, trees, and windows across the village. Mr. Harrison grieves the loss of his parrot Ginger, and Gilbert later visits Green Gables as the community takes stock of the destruction.

label: v2 · XXVIII The Prince Comes Back to the Enchanted Palace
value: Anne finishes her two-year term as the Avonlea schoolteacher.
chapter: v2 · XXVIII The Prince Comes Back to the Enchanted Palace

unit: In an irritable mood caused by a toothache, Anne has a terrible day at school, accidentally causing fireworks to explode in the classroom and later whipping Anthony Pye for putting a mouse in her desk. Returning home in despair, she confesses to Marilla, who comforts her and reassures her that everyone makes mistakes. The next day, Anne is amazed to find that whipping Anthony actually won his respect, a fact later confirmed by Mrs. Lynde.

chapter: v2 · XXVIII The Prince Comes Back to the Enchanted Palace

label: v2 · IV Different Opinions
value: Anne, Jane, and Gilbert debate teaching methods.
chapter: v2 · IV Different Opinions
unit: On the eve of the school year, Anne, Jane, and Gilbert debate teaching methods, particularly whether corporal punishment is ever justified. Anne walks home, stops to visit Mr. Harrison—who also doubts her gentle discipline approach—and goes to bed feeling anxious about her first day as a teacher. The next morning, Marilla comforts Anne and gives her advice before she sets off.

label: v2 · IX A Question of Color
value: Anne discusses with Mr. Harrison
chapter: v2 · IX A Question of Color
unit: Anne discusses Mrs. Lynde, truthfulness, and the Village Improvement Society's hall project with Mr. Harrison. Shortly after Joshua Pye finishes painting the hall, Mrs. Lynde discovers it was accidentally painted bright blue instead of green due to a mix-up with the paint numbers. Although the society members are devastated, the incident earns them widespread sympathy from the Avonlea community.

label: v2 · XIV A Danger Averted
value: Anne tries to convince Judson Parker not to rent his fences for patent medicine ads.
chapter: v2 · XIV A Danger Averted
unit: Anne, Diana, and Jane try to convince Judson Parker not to rent his fences for patent medicine ads, but he initially refuses. Later, Anne accidentally overhears Judson taking a political bribe from Jerry Corcoran. Fearing Anne will expose him and ruin his reputation, Judson agrees to cancel the ad contract in exchange for her silence, allowing Anne to report a successful outcome to the Improvers.

Returning home in despair, she confesses to Marilla, who comforts her and reassures her that everyone makes mistakes. The next day, Anne is amazed to find that whipping Anthony actually won his respect, a fact later confirmed by Mrs. Lynde.

chapter: v2 · XIV A Danger Averted
unit: Anne walks home with Mrs. Lynde, discussing community news and Marilla's improving eyesight. At Green Gables, Marilla and Anne learn that the twins' uncle cannot take them until autumn, and Anne helps correct Davy's funny theological misunderstandings after catching him eating plum jam. Later, at an Improvement Society meeting, the members are appalled to learn that Judson Parker plans to rent his fence to a patent medicine company for advertising, and Anne, Diana, and Jane fail to persuade him otherwise.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXIII. Anne Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
unit: During a game of dares at Diana's party, Anne accepts Josie Pye's challenge to walk the ridgepole of the kitchen roof, but she loses her balance and falls. During her seven weeks of recovery, Anne receives many visitors and looks forward to returning to school to meet the new teacher, Miss Stacy.

unit: Marilla returns home from an Aid meeting expecting tea, but finds that Anne has failed to prepare it and is hiding upstairs in despair. After washing fails to remove the dye, Marilla is forced to cut Anne's hair off, leading Anne to accept her punishment and resolve to focus on being good.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXIX. An Epoch in Anne’s Life
unit: Diana meets Anne in Lover's Lane to share the news that her Aunt Josephine has invited them to stay at her town home for the Exhibition. After getting Marilla's permission, Anne and Diana travel to Charlottetown with Mr. Barry, stay at Beechwood, and enjoy several days visiting the Exhibition, taking a drive in the park, and attending a concert. Upon returning home, Anne reflects happily on her wonderful trip and how good it is to be going back to Avonlea.

Upon arriving in town and starting her studies alongside fellow Avonlea students, she settles into her new boarding house. A visit from Josie, Jane, and Ruby reveals news of an Avery scholarship, inspiring Anne with ambitious new goals for her future.

label: v1 · CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
value: Anne discovers she has won the Avery scholarship.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream
unit: Anne discovers she has won the Avery scholarship while Gilbert Blythe wins the medal. After a celebratory commencement with Matthew, Marilla, and Aunt Josephine, Anne returns home to Green Gables and catches up with Diana. Soon after, Anne notices Matthew's failing health, learns from Marilla about their savings being tied up in a shaky bank, and shares a quiet, peaceful evening walk with Matthew.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXXVII. The Reaper Whose Name Is Death
unit: Matthew collapses from sudden heart failure caused by shock after reading news of the Abbey Bank's collapse, and dies instantly. Household members and community neighbors gather to mourn him, while Anne and Marilla try to comfort each other through their profound grief. In the following days, Anne confides her feelings to Mrs. Allan and later shares a quiet evening conversation with Marilla at Green Gables.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXXVIII. The Bend in the Road
unit: Marilla learns from an oculist that she must give up reading and sewing to save her failing eyesight, leading her to consider selling Green Gables. Anne decides to give up her college scholarship to stay home, care for Marilla, and teach at the local school. After learning that Gilbert Blythe gave up the Avonlea school position for her benefit, Anne reconciles with him, and they agree to become close friends.

chapter: v2 · I An Irate Neighbor
unit: Anne is daydreaming on her porch when Mr. Harrison furiously confronts her about her cow breaking into his oats. Anne retorts about his baldness before agreeing to keep the cow secured. Later, Anne, Marilla, and Mrs. Rachel Lynde discuss the encounter over tea alongside news of new residents moving into Avonlea.

chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: Anne and Diana discuss their plans for the Improvement Society while driving home from Carmody. Spotting a cow in Mr. Harrison's grain field, Anne hastily sells it to Mr. Shearer thinking it is her own cow, Dolly. Upon returning to Green Gables, Anne discovers Dolly is still in the pen and realizes she sold Mr. Harrison's cow by mistake, leading her to set off to apologize with a peace-offering cake.

Spotting a cow in Mr. Harrison's grain field, Anne hastily sells it to Mr. Shearer thinking it is her own cow, Dolly. Upon returning to Green Gables, Anne discovers Dolly is still in the pen and realizes she sold Mr. Harrison's cow by mistake, leading her to set off to apologize with a peace-offering cake.

chapter: v2 · III Mr. Harrison at Home
unit: Anne goes to Mr. Harrison's house to confess that she accidentally sold his Jersey cow instead of her own, and offers her own cow in exchange. chapter: v2 · IV Different Opinions
unit: On the eve of the school year, Anne, Jane, and Gilbert debate teaching methods, particularly whether corporal punishment is ever justified. Anne walks home, stops to visit Mr. Harrison—who also doubts her gentle discipline approach—and goes to bed feeling anxious about her first day as a teacher. The next morning, Marilla comforts Anne and gives her advice before she sets off.

unit: Marilla arrives home with the orphaned Keith twins, Davy and Dora, whose contrasting behaviors quickly manifest during dinner and bedtime. value: Anne has an irritable mood caused by a toothache.
chapter: v2 · XII A Jonah Day
unit: In an irritable mood caused by a toothache, Anne has a terrible day at school, accidentally causing fireworks to explode in the classroom and later whipping Anthony Pye for putting a mouse in her desk. Returning home in despair, she confesses to Marilla, who comforts her and reassures her that everyone makes mistakes. The next day, Anne is amazed to find that whipping Anthony actually won his respect, a fact later confirmed by Mrs. Lynde.

label: v2 · XIV A Danger Averted

chapter: v2 · XIV A Danger Averted
unit: Anne walks home with Mrs. Lynde, discussing community news and Marilla's improving eyesight. At Green Gables, Marilla and Anne learn that the twins' uncle cannot take them until autumn, and Anne helps correct Davy's funny theological misunderstandings after catching him eating plum jam. Later, at an Improvement Society meeting, the members are appalled to learn that Judson Parker plans to rent his fence to a patent medicine company for advertising, and Anne, Diana, and Jane fail to persuade him otherwise.

chapter: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
unit: After a newspaper item pokes fun at Uncle Abe's weather predictions, a sudden and devastating severe hail storm hits Avonlea on the exact day predicted. Anne and Marilla weather the storm at Green Gables with the twins, only to find extensive damage to crops, trees, and windows across the village. Mr. Harrison grieves the loss of his parrot Ginger, and Gilbert later visits Green Gables as the community takes stock of the destruction.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXIII. Anne Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor

During her seven weeks of recovery, Anne receives many visitors and looks forward to returning to school to meet the new teacher, Miss Stacy.

value: Marilla arrives home.
chapter: v2 · VIII Marilla Adopts Twins
unit: Marilla arrives home with the orphaned Keith twins, Davy and Dora, whose contrasting behaviors quickly manifest during dinner and bedtime. Davy creates chaos throughout his first week, first by dropping a caterpillar down a girl's neck at church and later by tricking Dora into falling into a pigpen before attempting to pump water on her. After being sent to bed, Davy confesses to Anne that he also placed a toad in Marilla's bed, which Anne frantically removes.

value: Marilla and Rachel Lynde attend a political meeting in Charlottetown.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XVIII. Anne to the Rescue
unit: While Marilla and Rachel Lynde attend a political meeting in Charlottetown, Anne and Matthew spend a quiet evening at Green Gables until Diana Barry rushes in desperately seeking help for her dangerously ill sister, Minnie May. Drawing on her past experience caring for infants, Anne treats Minnie May's croup throughout the night until the doctor arrives. The next day, Mrs. Barry relents on her former punishment, allowing Anne and Diana to resume their friendship.

unit: Anne convinces Marilla and Matthew to let her attend a concert and sleep over at Diana's house. After enjoying the concert, Anne and Diana race into the spare-room bed at Diana's house, accidentally jumping on Diana's formidable Aunt Josephine, who is enraged. Learning from Mrs. Lynde that Aunt Josephine plans to leave and cancel Diana's music lessons, Anne feels deeply remorseful for causing trouble.

value: Anne is in an irritable mood caused by a toothache.
chapter: v2 · XII A Jonah Day
unit: In an irritable mood caused by a toothache, Anne has a terrible day at school, accidentally causing fireworks to explode in the classroom and later whipping Anthony Pye for putting a mouse in her desk. Returning home in despair, she confesses to Marilla, who comforts her and reassures her that everyone makes mistakes. The next day, Anne is amazed to find that whipping Anthony actually won his respect, a fact later confirmed by Mrs. Lynde.

value: Anne returns from her last day of school
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
unit: Anne returns from her last day of school crying over Mr. Phillips's departure, despite her mixed feelings about him, and reports meeting Avonlea's new minister, Mr. Allan, and his wife. She later discusses the new minister with Matthew and Marilla, falls in love with Mrs. Allan as her new Sunday school teacher, and eagerly prepares to host the couple for tea at Green Gables. After preparing a layer cake and decorating the table, Anne watches in anticipation as Mrs. Allan and Marilla take their first bite of the cake, only for Marilla to react in shock.

value: Matthew notices that Anne dresses much more plainly than her peers.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXV. Matthew Insists on Puffed Sleeves
unit: Matthew notices that Anne dresses much more plainly than her peers and decides to buy her a pretty dress for Christmas. After a flustered encounter with a shop clerk, he enlists Mrs. Rachel Lynde to help select and sew a modern dress with puffed sleeves. On Christmas morning, Anne is overjoyed to receive the dress from Matthew and a pair of kid slippers from Aunt Josephine, making her performance at the school concert an absolute success.

unit: Diana meets Anne in Lover's Lane to share the news that her Aunt Josephine has invited them to stay at her town home for the Exhibition. Upon returning home, Anne reflects happily on her wonderful trip and how good it is to be going back to Avonlea.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out
unit: Anne and her classmates travel to town to take the Entrance examinations for Queen's Academy under Miss Stacy's guidance. After three nerve-wracking weeks of waiting back home in Avonlea, Diana brings the published pass list showing that Anne tied for first place on the entire island with Gilbert Blythe. Overjoyed, Anne shares the news with Matthew, Marilla, and Mrs. Lynde, and ends the day expressing deep gratitude for her success.

unit: Anne discovers she has won the Avery scholarship while Gilbert Blythe wins the medal. chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXXVII. The Reaper Whose Name Is Death
unit: Matthew collapses from sudden heart failure caused by shock after reading news of the Abbey Bank's collapse, and dies instantly. In the following days, Anne confides her feelings to Mrs. Allan and later shares a quiet evening conversation with Marilla at Green Gables.

A month later, news arrives that Richard Keith has died, leaving a trust fund for Davy and Dora, which ensures they can stay permanently at Green Gables.

label: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
value: A newspaper item pokes fun at Uncle Abe's weather predictions.
chapter: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
unit: After a newspaper item pokes fun at Uncle Abe's weather predictions, a sudden and devastating severe hail storm hits Avonlea on the exact day predicted. Anne and Marilla weather the storm at Green Gables with the twins, only to find extensive damage to crops, trees, and windows across the village. Mr. Harrison grieves the loss of his parrot Ginger, and Gilbert later visits Green Gables as the community takes stock of the destruction.

Spotting a cow in Mr. Harrison's grain field, Anne hastily sells it to Mr. Shearer thinking it is her own cow, Dolly. Upon returning to Green Gables, Anne discovers Dolly is still in the pen and realizes she sold Mr. Harrison's cow by mistake, leading her to set off to apologize with a peace-offering cake.

value: Marilla arrives home.
chapter: v2 · VIII Marilla Adopts Twins
unit: Marilla arrives home with the orphaned Keith twins, Davy and Dora, whose contrasting behaviors quickly manifest during dinner and bedtime. Davy creates chaos throughout his first week, first by dropping a caterpillar down a girl's neck at church and later by tricking Dora into falling into a pigpen before attempting to pump water on her. After being sent to bed, Davy confesses to Anne that he also placed a toad in Marilla's bed, which Anne frantically removes.

chapter: v2 · IX A Question of Color
unit: Anne discusses Mrs. Lynde, truthfulness, and the Village Improvement Society's hall project with Mr. Harrison. Shortly after Joshua Pye finishes painting the hall, Mrs. Lynde discovers it was accidentally painted bright blue instead of green due to a mix-up with the paint numbers. Although the society members are devastated, the incident earns them widespread sympathy from the Avonlea community.

The next day, Anne is amazed to find that whipping Anthony actually won his respect, a fact later confirmed by Mrs. Lynde.

label: CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid
value: Marilla returns home from an Aid meeting.
chapter: CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid
unit: Marilla returns home from an Aid meeting expecting tea, but finds that Anne has failed to prepare it and is hiding upstairs in despair. Anne reveals she bought hair dye from a traveling peddler to turn her red hair black, but it turned green instead. After washing fails to remove the dye, Marilla is forced to cut Anne's hair off, leading Anne to accept her punishment and resolve to focus on being good.

unit: Anne and her friends re-enact the story of Elaine, floating Anne down the pond in a flat. chapter: XXIX Poetry and Prose
unit: Anne finishes her two-year term as the Avonlea schoolteacher, prompting the local village women to gossip about the town's future, her pupils' love for her, and Stephen Irving's sudden arrival in town. Anne visits Paul and his father, Stephen Irving, who asks her to relay a message to Miss Lavendar. Anne delivers the message to Echo Lodge, where she and Charlotta help a nervous Miss Lavendar prepare for Stephen's arrival.

The following evening, Diana visits Green Gables to confide in Anne about her engagement, prompting Anne to reflect on love, change, and her own dreams for the future.
